I've been farming this land for 30 years. My father farmed before me. I know this land. I know what works.

My 10.9 mu goes wheat in autumn, maize in summer — same as always. That's how we do it here in Quzhou. Same land, two crops a year. I don't experiment. I grow what the market needs and what feeds my family.

**On wheat:** I'll plant improved varieties — the ones from the county seed station. Not the old varieties, those yields are too low. I put in phosphorus and potassium as base fertilizer when I till, then urea at jointing and again at heading. Three irrigations: one at sowing to get a good stand, one before winter sets in, one at jointing. Maybe one more at heading if it looks dry. I spray herbicide in spring when the weeds come up, and one fungicide spray near heading for rust. I use rotary tillage — I rented the machine last year and it works fine.

**On maize:** Right after wheat harvest I plant hybrid seeds, same ones most people around here use. I apply some fertilizer at planting and then top-dress urea at the big bell stage when the plant needs it most. Summer rains help but I still run the pump once or twice if it gets dry. One pesticide spray for borers. I let the stalk stay and rotary till it back in after harvest.

My wife and one son help during planting and harvest. The other son works in the city and sends money back. So I manage most of the season myself — I can't afford to do anything too complicated.
